title: The Indian rockets that ended up in the American anthem
hook: Rockets from India ended up in the American national anthem.
summary: Mysore's iron-cased rockets stunned the British in India, were copied by William Congreve, and were fired at Fort McHenry in 1814, inspiring "the rockets' red glare".
sources: Wikipedia: Mysorean rockets - iron-cased rockets used by Hyder Ali and Tipu Sultan; captured after Seringapatam 1799; influenced Congreve
Wikipedia: Congreve rocket - developed at Woolwich Arsenal from 1804; used at Fort McHenry 1814
Wikipedia: Battle of Pollilur (1780) - rocket hit British ammunition, causing explosion
Wikipedia: The Star-Spangled Banner - written by Francis Scott Key after the 1814 bombardment of Fort McHenry

lines.text: Rockets from India ended up in the American national anthem.
In seventeen eighty, Mysore fired iron-cased rockets at British troops.
One hit a gunpowder wagon, and the blast broke their lines.
In seventeen ninety-nine, the British captured the rockets and sent some to England.
In eighteen fourteen, ships fired his rockets at Baltimore.
A lawyer watching that night wrote about the rockets' red glare.
That song became the anthem, powered by an Indian idea.

post.caption:
Mysore's iron rockets scared the British, then inspired the weapon behind a famous line.
Would you have guessed the American anthem has an Indian link?
Follow @unt.oldfiles for a new untold story every day.
